newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Tunisia's Ben Ali starts Argentine visit.
newsitem.headline: Tunisia's Ben Ali starts Argentine visit.

text.p: Tunisian President Zine al-Abidine Ben Ali was welcomed by President Carlos Menem on Monday on the first day of a three-day official visit to Argentina to boost bilateral trade links.

Argentine officials said Menem met Ben Ali at Buenos Aires' metropolitan airport and reviewed troops with him. The two heads of state were scheduled to hold talks early on Tuesday, after which Ben Ali will visit the Argentine Congress.

Senior officials from both countries are due to sign a bilateral accord on Tuesday on cooperation on the environment, animal health, agriculture and on general economic, cultural and educational cooperation.

But diplomats say the thrust of trade conversations will be in energy, agriculture, tourism and shipping. Last week there was a trade mission to Tunis by Argentine oil company Pluspetrol, which has been explording for oil at the border between Tunisia and Libya since 1994.

Two-way trade between Tunisia and Argentina increased to $108 million in 1996 from just $28 million a year earlier. This is Ben Ali's first visit to Argentina, while Menem made visits to Tunisia in 1991 and 1994.
